If Indian demand slows, the Pacific outlet for US high-vol coal closes, the ~500kt a month of new US high-vol supply (management estimate) competes for Atlantic cargoes, and Alpha's realization falls toward the Atlantic level.
new: India steel demand slows. Alpha's Australian-indexed exports realized $143.82/t in Q2 FY2026 vs $109.08/t Atlantic. Without the Pacific outlet, new US high-vol supply competes for Atlantic cargoes and realization falls toward Atlantic levels.

new: Cost and liquidity. Highest cost in the basket: FY2026 Met cost guided $103–107/t vs $118.71/t realization. Fifth straight loss, LTM FCF ~zero, liquidity $447.8M. Each $10/t price drop costs ~$145M EBITDA, above $121M LTM.

The high-CV thermal leg partly hedges this, since PAMC sells into power and Indian cement rather than steel.
new: China electric-furnace steel accelerates. Met is 32% of CNR segment revenue but carries most bull-case upside. Weaker seaborne coking demand and a wider PLV–high-vol A spread hurt Leer; PAMC thermal partly hedges.

new: China electric-furnace steel accelerates. 50% of Warrior's Q2 FY2026 sales went to Asia. A structural shift cuts seaborne coking demand and pushes cheap Chinese steel into HCC's European and South American customers (35% and 14%).

old: Tariffs are a recurring cost that the FY2026 numbers hide. Management's FY2027 plan assumes a 15% incremental tariff from August 2026. Each 100bps of gross margin is ~$460M of EBIT, about 16% of FY2026 adjusted EBIT (~$2.8B). Nike's footwear is made mostly in Vietnam, Indonesia and China (hypothesis from prior 10-Ks, not re-checked), so a higher rate or a lost refund claim goes straight to margin.
new: Tariffs are a recurring cost hidden in FY2026: the $986M IEEPA refund added 210bps to gross margin (40.8% without). FY2027 assumes a 15% incremental tariff. Each 100bps of gross margin is ~$460M EBIT.

The Americas brand erosion is structural, not cyclical. The Americas are 69% of LTM revenue and 71% of FY2025 segment operating income, comps have been negative in all six quarters of FY2025 and FY2026 so far and reached -12% in Q2 FY2026, and the core leggings franchise fell ~20%. Competitors (Alo, Vuori, On) take the same premium customer.

Because stores, leases and marketing are fixed, every point of lost revenue falls through at a high rate: Q3 FY2026 operating margin is guided at ~6.5% vs 17% a year earlier. If Americas revenue falls to ~$6.2B, the bear case gives EPS of $7.69 and $76.86 a share, 21% below the price.

Metrics: (1) Q currency-neutral growth in Greater China, (2) signs of local traction, reported by Hill in "must-win doors" (high-single-digit sales growth in investment locations); and (3) stabilization of China EBIT (which fell from $1.60B to $1.28B between FY25 and FY26).
